rule: **C1 Symbol identity.** Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID: a call in the defining file, through an import, a re-export, an alias or a `require` binding. A definition that edges reach is listed in `nodes`, including body-less member declarations of scanned types (interface/trait/protocol methods) and module-level bindings that hold a function. A high edge's callee is always in `nodes`. | `crate::` paths and the package's own crate name resolve like module paths.
notes: Layout: src/ (the scan root) holds a Cargo package, Cargo.toml plus src/*.rs, so module paths are crate-relative. Package name `shapes`: main.rs reaches geometry.rs through `use shapes::geometry::{self, Point}` and the path shapes::geometry::spread; every reference uses the defining file's ID (Point#new, Point#dist, origin, spread). p: &Point → Point#dist (&T names the pointee); `let a = Point::new(..)` types a. `pub mod geometry;` is a declaration. call_type: SPEC lists direct|method without defining them; this corpus uses method for every callee of the form Type#m / recv.m / .m (including path calls Type::assoc()) and direct for free functions, module-path functions and named nested functions.
